# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles coordinates, spatial scope classifications and multi-decade population series for 1.880 assessed towns and metropolitan agglomerations across twelve East and Central African countries between 1961AD and 2025AD. Screened from 1.950 candidate municipal and urban entries (70 duplicate aliases excluded), the retained ledger spans 6.133 dated observations across 1.838 city-proper units and 42 metropolitan agglomerations. Active interpolated entries rise from 157 towns in 1961AD to 250 in 1991AD, 501 in 2000AD, 871 in 2015AD and 1.240 in 2025AD, documenting urban hierarchies from primate national capitals such as Nairobi, Dar es Salaam, Kampala, Kigali and Bujumbura down to rural market towns across Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi and adjacent border corridors.



# Background

Reconstructing urban settlement hierarchies in post-colonial East Africa requires harmonising statutory municipal census divisions with satellite-detected built-up footprints [@KNBS2019KenyaCensus; @NBSTanzania2022Census; @UBOS2024UgandaCensus; @OECD2024Africapolis]. Whereas administrative city limits in Nairobi, Dar es Salaam, Kampala, Kigali and Bujumbura capture core municipal districts, rapid peri-urban expansion after 1990AD pushed urban populations far beyond colonial town boundaries into surrounding counties and highland corridors [@Bank2012EastAfrican; @Bank2017RwandaEconomic; @Hayashi2007LongTerm]. Compiling both city-proper census series and metropolitan agglomerations within a single ledger preserves comparability across all twelve jurisdictions inside the East African study rectangle [@Tatem2007HighResolution; @Runfola2020GeoBoundaries].

# Methodology

## Candidate Screening and Territorial Scope

Candidate urban records were screened from KNBS, NBS/OCGS, UBOS, NISR and ISTEEBU census volumes, UNSD Demographic Yearbook tables and Africapolis [@KNBS2019KenyaCensus; @NBSTanzania2022Census; @UBOS2024UgandaCensus; @OECD2024Africapolis]. Of 1.950 candidates within the 1.743.957 km² study frame, 70 overlapping synonym records were merged or excluded, retaining 1.880 assessed settlements across 6.133 observations. Five core republics account for 1.735 entries - Tanzania (522), Uganda (519), Kenya (418), Burundi (198) and Rwanda (78) - alongside 145 adjacent border-zone towns in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (112), Malawi (10), Zambia (6), South Sudan (6), Somalia (4), Ethiopia (4) and Mozambique (3).

## Interpolation and Scope Conventions

Each entry reports either municipal city-proper populations (*City*) or continuous morphological agglomerations (*Metro*). Regional tables present linearly interpolated populations at four benchmark dates (1961AD, 1981AD, 2000AD and 2025AD) alongside each entry's peak population and peak year; benchmarks outside a town's observed span are marked with a hyphen (-). Notice that in densely farmed Lake Victoria, Mount Kenya, Mount Elgon and northern Burundi corridors, Africapolis morphological clusters merge extensive rural-urban settlements into multi-million conurbations (such as Kisumu, Embu, Mbale and Kayanza) that far exceed statutory town boundaries [@OECD2024Africapolis].

# Testing and Validation

Rank-size regression across the upper 180 urban peaks yields $q = 1,06$ ($R^2 = 0,99$), while full-sample regression across all 1.880 entries yields $q = 1,14$ ($R^2 = 0,95$), aligning closely with the 1.764 spatially deduplicated centres plotted in Figure \ref{fig:settlements-rank} [@Hayashi2007LongTerm; @OECD2024Africapolis]. Cross-checking city-proper and metropolitan entries confirms zero duplicate alias keys and clear separation between municipal and agglomeration series [@KNBS2019KenyaCensus; @UBOS2024UgandaCensus].

Table \ref{tab:gaz-rwanda} presents all 78 assessed settlements in Rwanda (77 city-proper and one metropolitan entry), led by Kigali (1,52M city-proper in 2022; 3,62M agglomeration in 2025AD), Gisenyi (1,47M), Ruhango (944,2k), Umutara (653,9k) and Rubavu (546,7k) [@Shipsey2022MakingThe; @Bank2017RwandaEconomic].

Table \ref{tab:gaz-burundi} records all 198 assessed settlements in Burundi (195 city-proper and three metropolitan entries), led by Bujumbura (497,2k city-proper in 2008; 2,25M agglomeration in 2025AD), Kayanza (3,86M northern highland agglomeration), Muyinga (620,2k) and Kirundo (492,1k) [@Verwimp2020ForcedDisplacement; @OECD2024Africapolis].

## Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo Border Corridor

Table \ref{tab:gaz-drc} lists 112 eastern Congolese towns falling inside the chapter bounding rectangle along Lakes Kivu, Edward and Tanganyika, led by Goma (1,77M), Bukavu (1,48M), Beni (481,6k) and Uvira (351,6k) [@OECD2024Africapolis].

# Limitations

Three caveats govern this gazetteer. First, combining city-proper census series with Africapolis morphological agglomerations means summed column totals across Tables \ref{tab:gaz-kenya} to \ref{tab:gaz-border} overlap where metropolitan entries encompass nested constituent towns. Second, linear interpolation leaves hyphens (-) outside each settlement's earliest and latest observed dates, so 1961AD counts (157 entries) understate smaller district towns first enumerated after 1990AD. Third, 145 cross-border towns lie outside the five East African republics and are omitted from national admin-1 area totals in the companion review.

# Conclusion

Together, the 1.880 entries in this gazetteer trace the post-colonial transformation of East Africa's urban network from 157 recorded towns in 1961AD to 1.240 active centres in 2025AD, documenting both statutory municipal growth and cross-border conurbation expansion across all twelve countries.
